mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25% over the next month, higher discount rates reduce the present value of future equity cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the identified FEDFUNDS rise (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS change < 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment) of at least 2,000 jobs coincides with stronger consumer demand, which elevates S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥2,000 in a month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant correlation with PAYEMS monthly increases (R² < 0.01).

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (retail sales) exceeds 1,800 in a month, it indicates resilient consumer demand, which is associated with positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite HOUST > 1,800 (p-value > 0.05 in out-of-sample test).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in INDPRO (industrial production) of 3% over two months signals supply-side weakness, which predicts negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by ≥3% over two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive during the identified INDPRO decline (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment) falls below 4.5% for three consecutive months, it signals labor market tightness that supports equity valuations, producing positive 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive during the UNRATE period (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in GDPC1 (GDP) and RSAFS (retail sales) of at least 2% in the same quarter indicate robust demand, leading to positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns through higher growth expectations.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 ↑ ≥2% and RSAFS ↑ ≥2% in the same quarter
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant correlation with the combined GDPC1-RSAFS increase (R² < 0.01).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in PAYEMS (job creation) of 5,000 or more in a month coincides with a bearish labor market, which is associated with negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases by ≥5,000 in a month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative during the PAYEMS drop (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent CPIAUCSL (inflation) increases above 3% for two consecutive months, the S&P 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to rate hike anticipation.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by >3% over two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite CPIAUCSL exceeding 3% for two months (p < 0.05 in falsification).
